Hi team — attaching initial artifacts and a short technical note. Attachments (stubbed here):
- hsm-attestation-202505.pdf (stub): vendor attestation from our HSM provider showing FIPS 140-2 level and key custody guarantees. Vendor signature embedded in PDF.
- rotation-log-sample-202507.csv (stub): anonymized rows showing key_id, rotated_at (ISO), rotation_trigger (scheduled/manual/alert), operator_hash (salted), previous_key_id.
- kms-config-extract.json (stub): sanitized extract of KMS config showing key policy templates, aliasing rules, and rotation window defaults.

Technical summary (short):
- In-transit: TLS 1.2 and TLS 1.3 supported; minimum accepted client TLS version is 1.2. Primary ciphers: TLS_AES_128_GCM_SHA256, TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384, ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256 (for 1.2 fallback). We enforce modern curves (P-256, X25519).
- At-rest: Customer data is encrypted with envelope encryption. Master KEKs are stored in HSM-backed KEK stores; DEKs are ephemeral and wrapped per request.
- Key rotation: default scheduled rotation window is 30 days for ephemeral table keys, 90 days for tenant KEKs. Emergency rekey process: 1) open incident ticket, 2) trigger rewrap job that rotates DEKs and pushes new KEK wraps to storage, 3) run validation job that compares checksums and sample decrypts. Rotation logs are immutable and retained for 13 months.
- Operator separation: HSM operator roles are split between operator_oncall and operator_admin groups; operator actions require two-person approval for critical KEK operations (policy enforced via HSM ACLs). No operator can extract plaintext keys from the HSM; keys are non-exportable.

I can join a technical call if you want to walk through the log sample.

— Aditya
Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.ai

Hi Alex — following up with the requested CAIQ mapping and some SOC2 pointers. Attached: caiq-mapping-parertech.xlsx (stub). Highlights:

- CAIQv3 mappings:
  - encr-1 (Data-in-transit): references TLS 1.2/1.3 + cipher suite list (see row 12).
  - encr-3 (Data-at-rest): references our envelope encryption description and HSM-backed KEKs (rows 21–24).
  - key-2 (Key lifecycle): maps to rotation policy, emergency rekey process, and retention (rows 30–34).

- SOC2: control CC6.1 (logical and physical access) and CC7.x (change management) are supported by our operator separation and immutable rotation logs. We can provide the relevant SOC2 control narrative excerpt under NDA if required.

- BYOK: we do support BYOK for tenant KEKs. Customers can supply an externally wrapped KEK; Redwood will store the wrapped KEK and perform non-exportable wraps in the HSM. Customer-driven rotation is supported on-demand; minimum recommended cadence for customer rotation is 90 days, but we can accept more frequent rotations subject to scheduling with Redwood infra if large-scale rewraps are needed.

I can provide the CAIQ mapping as an editable spreadsheet or a PDF. Happy to review the mapping on the Thurs 09:00 PT call if that works — Kimberly, Aditya, can you confirm availability?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
